title: The Hacker Ethic's MIT Origins
explainer: The informal code of conduct behind 'ethical hacking' traces back to MIT's Tech Model Railroad Club and AI Lab in the 1950s-60s, where journalist Steven Levy later identified a shared 'hacker ethic' in his 1984 book Hackers: Heroes of the Computer Revolution - values like hands-on exploration, sharing knowledge, and judging people by their skill rather than credentials. Knowing this history clarifies why the ethical-hacking community draws such a sharp line between curious, consent-based exploration and the unauthorized access the ground rules in this lesson exist to prevent.

title: WarGames (1983) and the Law Behind the Ground Rules
explainer: The US Computer Fraud and Abuse Act of 1986 - the law that makes unauthorized computer access a federal crime, and the reason scope-and-authorization paperwork matters before any lab exercise or real engagement - was motivated in part by the 1983 film WarGames, which reportedly led President Reagan to ask advisors whether a teenager could really hack into military computers. The result is the legal backbone separating a hacker practicing with permission from a felon: explicit, documented authorization.
